signals.name: No Access Authorization
signals.description: No policies and procedures exist for granting access to electronic protected health information (ePHI), including workstations, transactions, programs, and processes. signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Covered entities (healthcare providers, health plans, healthcare clearinghouses) Business associates handling ePHI Health information systems and EHR platforms Cloud service providers hosting ePHI IT infrastructure supporting healthcare operations

metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Verify that HHS notification procedures are documented in incident response plans Check for records of HHS breach portal submissions for breaches affecting 500+ individuals Ensure contemporaneous notification to HHS when individual notifications are sent for large breaches Review annual breach log submissions to HHS for breaches affecting fewer than 500 individuals Monitor that annual HHS notifications occur within 60 days after calendar year end Audit the use of HHS-specified notification methods and portal access Validate that both large (immediate) and small (annual) breach notifications are properly tracked

signals.name: No Individual Notification

metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Review incident response procedures to verify individual notification processes are defined and documented Examine breach incident logs and cross-reference with notification records to ensure all affected individuals were notified Verify that notification tracking systems capture all individuals whose PHI was compromised Check for automated notification workflows that trigger when breach thresholds are met Audit communication logs to confirm notification delivery to all affected parties Review business associate agreements to ensure notification responsibilities are clearly defined

metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Verify that a breach log system exists for tracking breaches affecting fewer than 500 individuals Review the breach log to ensure all small breaches are documented with required details Check that the log includes discovery dates, number of individuals affected, and breach descriptions Ensure the log is maintained in a secure, accessible location with appropriate access controls Audit the log for completeness by cross-referencing with incident reports and security event logs Verify that annual HHS submissions include all breaches from the log for the preceding year Monitor that logs are retained for the required period and are available for regulatory review

signals.name: No Media Notification (500+ affected)

metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Implement automated counting mechanisms to determine if 500+ individuals are affected Monitor breach incident reports for geographic distribution of affected individuals Verify that media notification procedures are triggered when the 500-person threshold is met Check for documented lists of "prominent media outlets" for each relevant state or jurisdiction Review records of media notifications including dates, outlets contacted, and content provided Audit incident response playbooks to ensure media notification steps are included for large breaches Validate that notification to media occurs within the same 60-day timeframe as individual notifications

metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Review breach notification templates to verify all five required elements are included Audit sent notifications against a compliance checklist to ensure completeness Check for standardized notification templates that enforce inclusion of required content Verify that notifications include specific dates (breach date and discovery date) Confirm that descriptions of compromised PHI types are sufficiently detailed Ensure protective steps for individuals are clearly outlined and actionable Validate that contact information for questions is prominently displayed and functional

Verify that records exist for repairs or changes to locks, doors, walls, access control systems, surveillance equipment, and other physical security components. Check for procedures requiring documentation before and after security-related maintenance activities.

metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Review media disposal and sanitization policies and procedures. Verify that documented processes exist for secure destruction or disposal of ePHI and storage media, including hard drives, backup tapes, CDs/DVDs, USB drives, and mobile devices. Check for procedures addressing physical destruction, degaussing, cryptographic erasure, or certified data destruction services with certificates of destruction.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart C - Physical Safeguards

metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Review procedures for sanitizing storage media before reallocation or repurposing. Verify that documented processes exist for securely removing ePHI from media intended for re-use, including formatting, wiping, or cryptographic erasure methods. Check for procedures addressing different media types and verification of successful data removal before media is reassigned or released.

metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Assess physical security controls for workstations accessing ePHI. Verify implementation of safeguards such as locking mechanisms, secure mounting, cable locks, proximity sensors, or placement in restricted access areas. Check for controls preventing unauthorized physical access to workstations, including laptop security, screen positioning, and automatic lock features when unattended.

Verify that documented procedures specify allowable functions for workstations accessing ePHI, proper usage protocols, and requirements for physical placement and surroundings. Check for policies addressing privacy screens, workstation positioning to prevent unauthorized viewing, and secure areas for workstations handling sensitive ePHI.

metadata.detection_notes: Detect access requests pending beyond the 30-day timeframe without proper extension notification, or requests that exceed the maximum 60-day response time (30 days plus one 30-day extension). Monitor request tracking systems for overdue access requests.

metadata.detection_notes: Detect absence of disclosure tracking mechanisms, incomplete accounting records, or failure to provide accounting within 60 days of request (with possible 30-day extension). Monitor for disclosure logs that do not capture required information (date, recipient, description, purpose).

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule
HHS Privacy Rule Guidance

signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Human resources and workforce management functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detect absence of amendment request processes, denied amendment requests without valid grounds for denial (record not created by entity, record not in designated record set, record not available for inspection, or record is accurate and complete), or systems lacking amendment request functionality.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal may occur when: PHI is used or disclosed without obtaining required written authorization Authorizations are missing required core elements (description of PHI, purpose, expiration, etc.) Authorizations lack required statements (right to revoke, treatment/payment not conditioned, etc.) Authorizations are obtained through defective notices or forms Authorizations are used beyond their expiration date Compound authorizations are improperly combined Revoked authorizations are not honored

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule
HHS Privacy Rule Guidance

signals.name: No Complaint Process
signals.description: No process for individuals to file privacy complaints.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Human resources and workforce management functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detect absence of documented complaint procedures, inaccessible complaint mechanisms, or missing complaint contact information in privacy notices. Verify that individuals have clear pathways to file complaints both internally and with HHS Office for Civil Rights.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule
HHS Privacy Rule Guidance

signals.name: No Confidential Communications
signals.description: No accommodation of requests for confidential communications.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Marketing and communications functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal may occur when: No process exists for individuals to request confidential communications Reasonable requests for alternative communication methods or locations are denied Healthcare providers improperly require explanations for confidential communication requests Health plans fail to accommodate requests when disclosure could endanger the individual Alternative addresses, phone numbers, or email addresses are not honored Systems are not configured to support confidential communication preferences Staff are not trained on confidential communication obligations Documentation of confidential communication requests and accommodations is inadequate

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule
HHS Privacy Rule Guidance

signals.name: No De-identification Standards
signals.description: No proper de-identification of health information using Expert Determination or Safe Harbor methods.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Marketing and communications functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal may occur when: De-identified data sets retain identifiers from the Safe Harbor list of 18 identifiers No expert determination has been obtained for de-identification methods Safe Harbor method is not properly applied with all required identifiers removed De-identification processes lack documentation or validation Re-identification risk assessments are not performed Limited data sets are created without proper data use agreements

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule
HHS Privacy Rule Guidance

signals.name: No Marketing Authorization
signals.description: PHI used for marketing without required authorization or disclosure of financial remuneration.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Marketing and communications functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal may occur when: Marketing communications are sent without obtaining required authorization Authorizations for marketing fail to disclose financial remuneration from third parties Treatment or health plan communications are mischaracterized to avoid marketing authorization requirements Refill reminders or health-related product recommendations contain marketing elements without authorization Face-to-face exception or nominal gift exception is improperly applied Financial incentives for marketing are not disclosed in authorizations

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule
HHS Privacy Rule Guidance

signals.name: No Minimum Necessary Standard
signals.description: No reasonable efforts to limit PHI to minimum necessary for the intended purpose.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Marketing and communications functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal may occur when: PHI disclosures include more information than necessary for the stated purpose Policies and procedures for minimum necessary determinations are absent or inadequate System configurations allow access to entire medical records when limited access would suffice Requests for PHI do not specify the minimum amount needed Regular reviews of minimum necessary practices are not conducted

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule
HHS Privacy Rule Guidance

signals.name: No Mitigation of Harmful Effects
signals.description: No mitigation of known harmful effects of privacy violations.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Human resources and workforce management functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detect known privacy violations without documented mitigation efforts, failure to address harmful effects of unauthorized disclosures, or absence of remediation actions following privacy incidents. Monitor incident response procedures for mitigation steps taken to reduce harm to affected individuals.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule
HHS Privacy Rule Guidance

signals.name: Incomplete Notice Content
signals.description: Notice of Privacy Practices does not contain all required elements.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Marketing and communications functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal may occur when: Notice lacks required header stating "THIS NOTICE DESCRIBES HOW MEDICAL INFORMATION ABOUT YOU MAY BE USED AND DISCLOSED..." Description of uses and disclosures is incomplete or inaccurate Individual rights section omits required rights (access, amendment, accounting, restrictions, confidential communications) Covered entity duties are not properly described Complaint procedures and contact information are missing or incomplete Effective date is absent or incorrect Required statements about marketing, fundraising, or sale of PHI are missing Notice does not describe state law protections that are more stringent than HIPAA

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule
HHS Privacy Rule Guidance

signals.name: No Notice Provision to Individuals
signals.description: Notice not provided at first service delivery, upon request, or as otherwise required.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Marketing and communications functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal may occur when: Notice is not provided at first service delivery to new patients or plan enrollees Notice is not provided promptly after emergency treatment Notice is not made available electronically when individuals access PHI through electronic means Good faith effort to obtain written acknowledgment is not documented Notice is not provided within required timeframes when material changes occur Notice is not posted in clear and prominent locations in facilities Notice is not available upon request Health plans fail to provide notice at enrollment or within 60 days of material revision

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule
HHS Privacy Rule Guidance

signals.name: No Privacy Contact Person
signals.description: No designated contact person/office for receiving complaints and providing information.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Human resources and workforce management functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detect absence of designated contact information in privacy notices, websites, or patient-facing materials. Verify that contact person/office information is current and accessible to individuals seeking to file complaints or obtain privacy information.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule
HHS Privacy Rule Guidance

signals.name: No Notice of Privacy Practices
signals.description: No Notice of Privacy Practices provided to individuals.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Marketing and communications functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal may occur when: Covered entities fail to develop or maintain a Notice of Privacy Practices Notice is not available for distribution to individuals Notice has not been updated to reflect material changes in privacy practices Electronic notice availability requirements are not met for entities with web presence Notice is not available in the language or format needed by the individual population served Documentation of notice provision is not maintained

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule
HHS Privacy Rule Guidance

signals.name: No Designated Privacy Official
signals.description: No designated privacy official responsible for privacy policies and procedures.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Human resources and workforce management functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detect absence of documented privacy official designation, vacancy in the privacy official role, or organizational documentation lacking privacy officer identification. Review organizational charts, policy documents, and privacy notices for privacy official designation.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule
HHS Privacy Rule Guidance

signals.name: No Privacy Training
signals.description: No training provided to workforce members on privacy policies and procedures.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Human resources and workforce management functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detect workforce members without documented privacy training, new hires not trained within reasonable timeframes, or absence of training updates following material policy changes. Monitor training completion records, onboarding processes, and retraining after policy updates.

HHS Privacy Rule Guidance

signals.name: No Psychotherapy Notes Protection
signals.description: Psychotherapy notes used or disclosed without required authorization.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Marketing and communications functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal may occur when: Psychotherapy notes are disclosed without specific authorization separate from other PHI authorizations Psychotherapy notes are improperly commingled with general medical records Notes that do not meet the definition of psychotherapy notes are incorrectly segregated Psychotherapy notes are used for purposes beyond the narrow exceptions (originator's treatment use, training, legal defense, oversight) Providers fail to maintain separate storage and access controls for psychotherapy notes

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule
HHS Privacy Rule Guidance

signals.name: No Rights to Request Restrictions
signals.description: Individuals not permitted to request restrictions on uses and disclosures of their PHI.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Marketing and communications functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal may occur when: Individuals are prevented from making restriction requests No process exists for receiving and tracking restriction requests Required restrictions (out-of-pocket payment in full) are not honored Agreed-upon restrictions are not implemented in systems or workflows Restrictions are not properly documented Terminated restrictions are not properly communicated to affected parties Emergency circumstances exception to restrictions is improperly applied Restriction request denials are not properly documented or communicated

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule
HHS Privacy Rule Guidance

signals.name: No Retaliation Protection
signals.description: Intimidation or retaliation against individuals exercising their privacy rights.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Human resources and workforce management functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detect adverse actions taken against individuals who exercised privacy rights, filed complaints, or participated in investigations. Monitor for patterns of denials of service, increased costs, or other retaliatory measures following privacy-related activities. Review complaints alleging intimidation or retaliation.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule
HHS Privacy Rule Guidance

signals.name: No Administrative/Technical/Physical Safeguards
signals.description: No appropriate administrative, technical, and physical safeguards to protect PHI.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Human resources and workforce management functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detect absence of documented safeguards, inadequate access controls, lack of physical security measures, or insufficient technical protections for PHI. Evaluate administrative policies, technical security controls (encryption, authentication, audit logs), and physical security measures (locked files, secure facilities, visitor controls).

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule
HHS Privacy Rule Guidance

signals.name: No PHI Sale Prohibition
signals.description: PHI disclosed for remuneration without proper authorization.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Marketing and communications functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal may occur when: PHI is disclosed in exchange for direct or indirect remuneration without authorization Authorization for sale of PHI does not explicitly state that remuneration is involved Exceptions for public health purposes, research, treatment/payment, business associate services, or individual-requested disclosures are improperly applied Financial arrangements involving PHI disclosure are not properly documented Data brokers or third parties receive PHI in exchange for payment without proper authorization Reasonable cost-based fees are exceeded, constituting remuneration

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule
HHS Privacy Rule Guidance

signals.name: No Sanctions for Non-Compliance
signals.description: No sanctions applied against workforce members for privacy violations.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Human resources and workforce management functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detect absence of documented sanction policies, failure to apply sanctions for confirmed privacy violations, or lack of enforcement of privacy policies. Review incident response records, disciplinary actions, and workforce accountability measures for privacy non-compliance.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule
HHS Privacy Rule Guidance

signals.name: No Treatment/Payment/Operations Limits
signals.description: Uses and disclosures for treatment, payment, or health care operations exceed permitted scope.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Marketing and communications functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal may occur when: PHI is disclosed for treatment beyond what is necessary for coordinating care Payment-related disclosures exceed billing and reimbursement purposes Health care operations uses go beyond permitted activities (quality assessment, training, accreditation, etc.) TPO purposes are broadly interpreted to justify inappropriate disclosures Notice of Privacy Practices does not adequately describe TPO uses and disclosures

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule
HHS Privacy Rule Guidance

signals.name: No Limits on Uses and Disclosures
signals.canonical_name: No Limits on Uses and Disclosures
signals.description: No limits on uses and disclosures of PHI; disclosures made beyond permitted or required purposes.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Marketing and communications functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal may occur when: PHI is used or disclosed for purposes not explicitly permitted by HIPAA Disclosures are made without proper authorization or legal basis PHI is shared beyond the scope of permitted purposes Monitoring reveals uses and disclosures that exceed regulatory permissions

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule
HHS Privacy Rule Guidance

signals.name: No Waiver Prohibition
signals.description: Individuals required to waive rights as condition of treatment, payment, or benefits.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Healthcare providers with direct patient relationships Health plans and insurers Healthcare clearinghouses Business associates handling PHI Patient-facing systems and portals Human resources and workforce management functions

metadata.detection_notes: Detect forms, agreements, or policies requiring waiver of access rights (164.524) or accounting of disclosures rights (164.528) as a condition of receiving treatment, payment, plan enrollment, or benefits eligibility. Review consent forms, enrollment documents, and service agreements for prohibited waiver language.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E - Privacy Rule
HHS Privacy Rule Guidance

signals.name: No Audit Controls
signals.description: No hardware, software, or procedural mechanisms to record and examine activity in systems containing ePHI.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Electronic health record (EHR) systems Health information exchanges (HIEs) Patient portals and healthcare applications Database systems containing ePHI Network infrastructure transmitting ePHI Cloud services hosting healthcare data

metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Review system logging configurations and audit trail capabilities. Verify that systems capture user access, modifications, deletions, and other activities involving ePHI. Check for centralized log management, log retention policies, and regular audit log reviews. Identify systems with disabled logging or insufficient audit trail detail.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart C - Technical Safeguards
NIST SP 800-66 Rev 2 - Implementing the HIPAA Security Rule
HHS Security Rule Guidance

signals.name: No Person or Entity Authentication
signals.description: No procedures to verify that a person or entity seeking access to ePHI is the one claimed.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Electronic health record (EHR) systems Health information exchanges (HIEs) Patient portals and healthcare applications Database systems containing ePHI Network infrastructure transmitting ePHI Cloud services hosting healthcare data

metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Evaluate authentication mechanisms including password policies, multi-factor authentication, biometric systems, and certificate-based authentication. Check for weak authentication methods such as simple passwords without complexity requirements, absence of account lockout policies, or systems that do not properly verify user credentials before granting access to ePHI.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart C - Technical Safeguards
NIST SP 800-66 Rev 2 - Implementing the HIPAA Security Rule
HHS Security Rule Guidance

signals.name: No Automatic Logoff
signals.description: No electronic procedures to terminate sessions after predetermined period of inactivity.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Electronic health record (EHR) systems Health information exchanges (HIEs) Patient portals and healthcare applications Database systems containing ePHI Network infrastructure transmitting ePHI Cloud services hosting healthcare data

metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Test application and system session timeout settings to verify automatic logoff functionality. Check for configured idle timeout periods in web applications, terminal sessions, and database connections. Monitor for systems that allow indefinite session persistence or require manual logout only.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart C - Technical Safeguards
NIST SP 800-66 Rev 2 - Implementing the HIPAA Security Rule
HHS Security Rule Guidance

signals.name: No Emergency Access Procedure
signals.description: No procedures for obtaining necessary ePHI during an emergency.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Electronic health record (EHR) systems Health information exchanges (HIEs) Patient portals and healthcare applications Database systems containing ePHI Network infrastructure transmitting ePHI Cloud services hosting healthcare data

metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Review system documentation and incident response procedures to verify the existence of emergency access protocols. Check for documented procedures that allow authorized personnel to access ePHI during system failures, disasters, or other emergency situations. Verify that emergency access mechanisms are tested and that access is properly logged and audited.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart C - Technical Safeguards
NIST SP 800-66 Rev 2 - Implementing the HIPAA Security Rule
HHS Security Rule Guidance

signals.name: No Encryption and Decryption
signals.description: No mechanism to encrypt and decrypt ePHI.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Electronic health record (EHR) systems Health information exchanges (HIEs) Patient portals and healthcare applications Database systems containing ePHI Network infrastructure transmitting ePHI Cloud services hosting healthcare data

metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Examine data storage configurations, database encryption settings, and file system encryption status. Check for unencrypted ePHI at rest on servers, workstations, portable devices, and backup media. Verify encryption standards and key management practices for systems that do implement encryption.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart C - Technical Safeguards
NIST SP 800-66 Rev 2 - Implementing the HIPAA Security Rule
HHS Security Rule Guidance

signals.name: No ePHI Integrity Mechanism
signals.description: No electronic mechanisms to corroborate that ePHI has not been altered or destroyed in an unauthorized manner.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Electronic health record (EHR) systems Health information exchanges (HIEs) Patient portals and healthcare applications Database systems containing ePHI Network infrastructure transmitting ePHI Cloud services hosting healthcare data

metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Examine systems for integrity verification mechanisms such as digital signatures, hash functions, checksums, or blockchain technologies. Review change management processes and version control systems for ePHI. Check for file integrity monitoring tools and database audit trails that detect unauthorized modifications.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart C - Technical Safeguards
NIST SP 800-66 Rev 2 - Implementing the HIPAA Security Rule
HHS Security Rule Guidance

signals.name: No Transmission Encryption
signals.description: No mechanism to encrypt ePHI whenever deemed appropriate during transmission.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Electronic health record (EHR) systems Health information exchanges (HIEs) Patient portals and healthcare applications Database systems containing ePHI Network infrastructure transmitting ePHI Cloud services hosting healthcare data

metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Analyze network traffic and communication channels for unencrypted ePHI transmission. Check for proper implementation of TLS/SSL for web applications, VPN usage for remote access, and encrypted protocols for file transfers (SFTP, FTPS). Verify that email containing ePHI uses encryption (S/MIME, PGP, or secure email gateways) and that API communications use HTTPS.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart C - Technical Safeguards
NIST SP 800-66 Rev 2 - Implementing the HIPAA Security Rule
HHS Security Rule Guidance

signals.name: No Transmission Integrity Controls
signals.description: No security measures to ensure electronically transmitted ePHI is not improperly modified without detection.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Electronic health record (EHR) systems Health information exchanges (HIEs) Patient portals and healthcare applications Database systems containing ePHI Network infrastructure transmitting ePHI Cloud services hosting healthcare data

metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Review network transmission protocols and security measures for ePHI transfers. Check for integrity verification mechanisms such as message authentication codes (MACs), digital signatures, or secure protocols (TLS/SSL) that include integrity checking. Verify that file transfers, API communications, and messaging systems implement tamper detection.

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart C - Technical Safeguards
NIST SP 800-66 Rev 2 - Implementing the HIPAA Security Rule
HHS Security Rule Guidance

signals.name: No Unique User Identification
signals.description: No unique name and/or number assigned for identifying and tracking user identity.
signals.applicability: This signal applies to: Electronic health record (EHR) systems Health information exchanges (HIEs) Patient portals and healthcare applications Database systems containing ePHI Network infrastructure transmitting ePHI Cloud services hosting healthcare data

metadata.detection_notes: Detection guidance: Examine user account configurations, authentication systems, and access logs to verify that each user has been assigned a unique identifier. Look for shared accounts, generic usernames (e.g., "admin", "user"), or systems that allow multiple users to authenticate with the same credentials.
